, Reason for Mistake: The agent failed to correctly simulate the game mechanics. It incorrectly assumed that the first ball (Ball 1) is always in the firing position or has the highest probability of being ejected. In reality, the balls cycle through positions 1, 2, and 3 based on which piston fires. Ball 1 is only ejected if Piston 1 fires while it is in Position 1. If Piston 2 or 3 fires first, Ball 1 moves to Position 2 or is released/shifted, changing its fate. The optimal strategy involves calculating the probability of a ball reaching Position 1 before being skipped over or released, which actually favors Ball 3 in this specific setup due to the shifting dynamics where Ball 3 has a higher chance of landing in the "sweet spot" of being ejected early before the queue shifts it away. The agent's logic that "the first ball... is always in the position to be ejected first" is factually incorrect regarding the random nature of the piston firing.
